notes: ncert.nic.in (textbook.php and the textbook PDF/prelims files) refused automated fetching (robots.txt disallow) on 2026-10-19, so the NCERT contents pages, printed section headings and edition/reprint lines could not be read directly. Chapter titles were verified instead against other official government sources: NCERT's CIET audio-book pages (ciet.ncert.gov.in) and the Delhi Directorate of Education 2026-27 syllabus (edustud.nic.in), which prescribes NCERT books. 'verified': true means the title was seen in at least one of those sources.

CBSE does not publish its own mathematics syllabus for Grades 6-8. Its 2026-27 curriculum release (Circular Acad-14/2026) covers Classes IX-XII only, and CBSE circulars direct schools to the new NCERT textbooks. The 2026-27 prescription is therefore inferred from those circulars plus the Delhi DoE 2026-27 syllabus. No CBSE or NCERT notice found replaces or withdraws Ganita Prakash for 2026-27.

Section titles come from the subtopic lists in the Delhi DoE 2026-27 annual syllabus, not from the printed textbook. They appear to quote the textbook's section headings, but DoE may have shortened, merged or left some out (its list is 'for assessment purpose only'), and capitalisation follows DoE. Check them against the printed NCERT book before using them as exact headings.

Learning outcomes are written by the compiler from the chapter and section scope. They are not copied from NCERT's Learning Outcomes document, which was not consulted because ncert.nic.in was inaccessible.

Secondary sites (teachoo.com, edzy.ai, esaral.com, aglasem.com, collegedunia.com) were used only to locate official documents and to cross-check chapter order and titles. Nothing was taken from them as authoritative.

Grade 7: the new NCERT Grade 7 mathematics book came in from 2025-26 (CBSE Circular Acad-12/2025) in two parts: Ganita Prakash Part I (8 chapters) and Part II (7 chapters). The Delhi DoE 2026-27 Grade 7 syllabus prescribes Part I (Ch 1-8) and Part II (Ch 1-7), which confirms both parts are in use in 2026-27.

Chapter numbering starts again at 1 in Part II. Here 'term' records the book part (1 = Part I, 2 = Part II), and chapter ids follow the term-book pattern (cbse-g07-t1-c01 ... cbse-g07-t2-c07). In the Delhi DoE plan Part I is taught before the mid-term and Part II after it. CBSE itself does not set terms for Grade 7.

Grade 7 chapter titles: the official CIET pages show them only as audio file names (underscores, no punctuation). Punctuation and capitalisation (e.g. 'Expressions using Letter-Numbers', 'Connecting the Dots' — secondary sites print 'Connecting the Dots...') follow the DoE syllabus and secondary sites, and should be checked against the printed contents page.
Part I edition: assumed to be the first edition of 2025 (released for 2025-26). The imprint line was not seen. For Part II, the NCERT catalogue gives publication year 2025 but no edition statement.

Part II Ch 2 (Operations with Integers): DoE lists only 'A Quick Recap of Integers' and 'Multiplication of Integers'. Whether the chapter also covers division of integers was not verified, so no division outcome is included. If division is in the book, add it under MATH.number.integer-multiply (or a separate division competency).

Part II Ch 3 (Finding Common Ground): the 'Pretty Procedure' is probably an HCF algorithm (possibly Euclid's division method), but this was not verified. The outcome is mapped only partially to MATH.number.euclid-algorithm.

Part II Ch 6 (Constructions and Tilings): DoE lists only 'Geometric Constructions' and 'Tiling', so the specific constructions taught (e.g. perpendicular or angle bisectors, regular polygons) are not known. The construction outcome is deliberately general.
Part II Ch 5 (Connecting the Dots): whether mode, range or double bar graphs are included was not verified. The outcomes cover only mean/median and general graph choice.

outcomes.statement: Read, write and compare numbers up to crores in the Indian system and convert them to and from the international system (millions, billions).

proposed.why: MATH.number.large-numbers is about reading/comparing; lakh-crore vs million-billion naming and conversion is a separate assessed skill.

outcomes.statement: Explain place value as repeated groupings of ten (e.g. how many thousands make a lakh, how many lakhs make a crore).

outcomes.statement: Use patterns in products (e.g. multiplying by powers of ten) to calculate and estimate large products and to judge the size of large quantities.

outcomes.statement: Compare or rewrite expressions without fully evaluating them by swapping and grouping terms and handling signs when removing brackets.

outcomes.statement: Represent tenths, hundredths and thousandths in decimal notation and state the place value of each digit.

sections.title: Omission of the Multiplication Symbol in Algebraic Expressions

outcomes.statement: Use letters for unknown or varying quantities to write algebraic expressions for situations.
Evaluate algebraic expressions for given values of the letters.

Describe patterns (e.g. in matchstick figures or calendars) with algebraic expressions and use them to reveal relationships.

proposed.name: Express and justify a general pattern with an algebraic expression
proposed.why: MATH.algebra.pattern-rules is in words (Grade 4) and MATH.algebra.variables is evaluation; writing an algebraic generalisation of a pattern or trick and using it to justify the pattern is not covered.

sections.title: Parallel and Perpendicular Lines in Paper Folding

outcomes.statement: Use the facts that angles in a linear pair add to 180 degrees and that vertically opposite angles are equal to find unknown angles where two lines cross.

proposed.name: Use linear pairs, vertically opposite, complementary and supplementary angles
proposed.why: MATH.geometry.parallel-angles is about angles made by a transversal with parallel lines; relationships between angles at a single intersection are not covered.

outcomes.statement: Identify perpendicular and parallel lines, and make them by paper folding.
Name the corresponding and alternate angles made by a transversal and use them to find unknown angles when the lines are parallel.
Use angle conditions to decide whether two lines are parallel and justify the decision.
Draw a line parallel to a given line through a given point using geometric tools.

sections.title: Nature's Favourite Sequence: The Virahāṅka–Fibonacci Numbers!

outcomes.statement: Predict and justify whether a sum, difference or product is even or odd without calculating it.

proposed.name: Reason with parity of sums and products
proposed.why: No existing competency covers predicting/justifying whether sums and products are even or odd, a recurring Ganita Prakash theme (Grade 7 'Picking Parity', Grade 8 'Exploring Even and Odd Sums').

outcomes.statement: Solve and reason about grid puzzles such as magic squares with given row, column and diagonal sums.

proposed.name: Solve number grid puzzles such as supercells and magic squares
proposed.why: Grid-based number reasoning (supercells, magic squares, grid sums) is assessed in Number Play chapters and is not covered by any existing competency.

outcomes.statement: Generate Virahanka-Fibonacci numbers, link them to counting problems (e.g. rhythms of short and long beats), and explore their patterns.

proposed.name: Generate and reason about recursively defined sequences
proposed.why: Virahanka-Fibonacci numbers (each term the sum of the previous two) are a recursive sequence; existing pattern/progression competencies are additive or arithmetic/geometric.

outcomes.statement: Work out the hidden digits in letter-coded addition or multiplication puzzles.

proposed.name: Solve cryptarithm (digits-in-disguise) puzzles
proposed.why: Deducing hidden digits in letter-coded arithmetic uses place value and carrying in a way no existing competency describes.
